item.title: Music Beneath the Radio Calls

turns.text: Add a tense instrumental bed to this. Keep it under the radio calls so every word is easy to hear, especially 'Rook, you with me?' Don't change the footage.

item.tests: Tests whether added music remains audibly subordinate to the original speech, with intelligibility preserved throughout the delivered video.

answer_sheet.Music mood and vocals: Tense instrumental music, with no singing.
answer_sheet.Music level relative to speech: Clearly quieter than the radio calls whenever someone speaks; every original word must remain easy to hear.
answer_sheet.Source footage, duration, and framing: Keep the entire attached 7-second cockpit clip, with unchanged visuals, timing, and framing.
answer_sheet.Speech and added text: Keep the original radio-call recording in sync. Do not replace it or add text.

must_haves: The output preserves all seven seconds of the original cockpit footage without visual changes or extra shots.
A tense instrumental music bed is audible, with no added singing.
The original radio calls remain present and synchronized, including the clearly intelligible line 'Rook, you with me?'
During every spoken line, the music is perceptibly below the voice and does not mask words with loud beats, swells, or accents.
The music is not simply muted for the entire clip; it is audible while remaining subordinate to speech.

turns.text: Add a tense instrumental bed to this. Keep it under the radio calls so every word is easy to hear, especially 'Rook, you with me?' Don't change the footage.

dialog.agent:
I can generate a tense instrumental track, but the connected tools can’t mix it beneath your existing radio audio while leaving the footage untouched. I haven’t changed your video.

If you’d like a separate music bed, tell me the clip’s duration. When mixing, duck the music during every radio call—especially **“Rook, you with me?”**—to keep the words clear.
dialog.why: It says the connected tools cannot mix music beneath the existing radio audio while preserving the footage, and confirms the video was not changed. The request for duration is only for an alternative separate music bed.
dialog.user: Please go ahead with the free settings anyway.

dialog.why: It asks the user to specify the duration and waits for an answer.

dialog.agent:
The music generator’s minimum is **15 seconds**, so it can’t make an exact 7-second track. Should I generate a 15-second tense instrumental for you to trim to 7 seconds?

It would be a separate audio file; I still can’t mix it under the radio calls with these tools. Your footage will remain unchanged.
dialog.why: It asks for confirmation to proceed with generating a 15-second instrumental as an alternative, and waits.

turns.agent:
The account refused the generation because it has **insufficient credits**. No music was created, and your video is unchanged.

The 15-second instrumental requires **15 credits**. Once those are available, we can retry.
